tools.name: render-markdown
tools.description:
Convert a Markdown source string to an HTML string using marked v12.0.2 (parse). Supports headings, lists, fenced code, blockquotes, links, images, emphasis, and GFM extensions (tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks). Params: markdown (string, required, the Markdown source); gfm (bool, optional, default true, enable GitHub-flavored Markdown); breaks (bool, optional, default false, requires gfm, convert single line breaks to
); pedantic (bool, optional, default false, conform to markdown.pl quirks). Returns the rendered HTML as text.

tools.name: render-markdown-inline
tools.description:
Convert an inline Markdown fragment (no block-level elements) to HTML without an enclosing

tag using marked v12.0.2 parseInline. Best for short spans such as '**bold** text', '`code`', or 'a [link](https://example.com)' — returns raw inline HTML like bold text. Params: markdown (string, required, the inline fragment); gfm (bool, optional, default true). Returns the inline HTML as text.

tools.name: tokenize-markdown
tools.description: Lex a Markdown source string into its parsed token stream and return it as a JSON array using the marked v12.0.2 lexer. Each token has a 'type' (heading, paragraph, list, code, table, text, strong, link, ...) plus type-specific fields (raw, text, depth, tokens, ...). Useful for inspecting how Markdown parses, counting structure, or feeding tokens to a later stage. Params: markdown (string, required, the Markdown source). Returns a JSON-formatted array of tokens as text.
